scope: Malta · civil and criminal proceedings (separately scoped references)

esig_regulation.basis: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 applies directly. Cap. 426, art. 9: an electronic contract is not denied legal effect, validity or enforceability solely because it is wholly or partly electronic. The national provisions supplementing eIDAS were not verified.

data_access_basis.basis: A private party needs a lawful basis under GDPR Art. 6(1), for example legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)); data on criminal offences needs official authority or a legal authorisation (Art. 10). A person can request their own data (Art. 15) within the Art. 12(3) period. Processing by competent authorities for criminal offences is governed by S.L. 586.08, which transposes Directive (EU) 2016/680.

timestamp_recognition.basis: Art. 41(1): a time stamp is not denied legal effect or admissibility solely because it is electronic or not qualified. Art. 41(2): a qualified time stamp is presumed accurate as to date and time and integrity of the bound data. Art. 42(1) sets the qualified requirements; Art. 24a(6) recognises qualified time stamps across Member States.

evidence_rules.basis: The court requires the best evidence the party can produce and disallows evidence it considers irrelevant, superfluous or not the best available.

Authentic copies of the documents listed in arts. 627, 628 and 629(a)-(c) and (e), such as acts of the Government of Malta and of foreign governments and courts, are admissible and are evidence to the same extent as the originals.
The fullest and most satisfactory proof available must be produced, without omitting any important witness; the testimony of one witness, if believed, can be sufficient proof.

sources.term: Code of Organization and Civil Procedure (Cap. 12)
